text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 3.55% today as oil prices surged to six-month highs on escalating Middle East tensions. Brent crude topped $116 per barrel—driven by U.S.-Iran friction, Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure, and Trump administration warnings of potential action against Iran. The company benefits directly: as a major oil producer, higher crude prices flow straight to the bottom line, and the geopolitical risk premium built into oil valuations lifts all upstream players.

The two-week gain of 12.45% shows this is part of a sustained energy rally, not a one-day blip. News over the past week consistently tied rising oil prices to Middle East conflict risks and U.S. policy shifts, which have kept the sector in favor as investors rotate into energy beneficiaries of the broader "Iran war" reshaping global markets.
